notes: Lost Land Adventure (64-bit UE4 title behind RSLauncher.exe, 2026-10-21). The launcher and LLA/Binaries/Win64/DomeShooterGame-Win64-Shipping.exe both load hasp_windows_x64_106993.dll -- the exact name our emulator is built as -- so our DLL replaces the vendor runtime through the drop-in (WINEDLLOVERRIDES hasp_windows_x64_106993=n, RAVENGUN_HASP_DIR=ravengun-hasp, RAVENGUN_HASP_GAME=LostLandAdventure, RAVENGUN_HASP_VERBOSE=1). The values here are SYNTHETIC, built from what the game itself asks for, never from TeknoParrot: the haspid is invented, the features/keycaps are the standard HASP HL set and the 112-byte read/write image is zero-filled, because RSLauncher writes (hasp_write) and the game reads back, so the round trip is consistent without any real dongle data. The memory size is the first value tried; RAVENGUN_HASP_VERBOSE=1 logs every call so it can be corrected from the game's own requests. READ-ONLY IMAGE (fileid 65520 = 0xFFF0, 2026-10-21), built only from the game's own code: DomeShooterGame-Win64-Shipping.exe 0x140a2ade0 logs in (feature 0xFFFF0000), reads 64 bytes at offset 0xD00 of fileid 0xFFF0, calls hasp_decrypt on them (our decrypt leaves the buffer as is, so the image holds the plain record), requires byte 0x3F == ~byte 0x3E, copies bytes 0..12 out and compares them with the region's serial pattern ('*' = any byte); the result goes to RSDongleHandler.Result.ErrorCode, and DSGameInfo.CheckDongle starts DOME_FatalError (the FATAL ERROR screen) when it is not DESC_VALID. The patterns are the SerialNumberPatterns defaults of Default__DSDongleHandler in DomeShooterGame.u (JAPAN '27281*15****', FOREIGN '27282*15****', CHINA '27285*15****'); the pattern is chosen by RSDongleHandler::SetDongleSettingFromLang (0x140a1b2b0): language INT -> index 1 (JAPAN) on the USB finder (no HASP), CHN/CHT -> index 5 (CHINA), anything else -> index 2 (FOREIGN) on HASP; RSLauncher starts the game with -Language=JPN, so the record is the invented serial '272820150001' + NUL (byte 4 = region 2, byte 5 = RevenueCode digit 0), bytes 0x3E/0x3F = 00/FF, the rest zero; size 3392 = 0xD00 + 0x40, the highest byte the code reads.
